expectations.text: B1: Gives an honest constraint (fork/exec/pipes are POSIX) and offers a concrete workable option instead of pretending it works natively
expectations.evidence: Honest constraint given: C tutorials "need `fork`/`waitpid`/`dup2`, which MinGW lacks" and "Windows has no POSIX signals or job control"; concrete workable options offered (A: Go/Rust native via "`exec.Command` / `std::process::Command` replaces fork+exec", B: MSYS2/Cygwin, C: Linux VM/Codespaces) instead of claiming native support.

expectations.text: B2: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: a concrete command to run and the expected output/behaviour
expectations.evidence: Answer ends with "Which language are you comfortable in? Default if you have no preference: Go — the standard library covers every milestone except signals with zero extra dependencies." — no concrete command to run and no expected output/behaviour.

expectations.text: B3: States that fork() is not available on native Windows and suggests WSL, a Linux VM/container, or CreateProcess-based alternative with trade-offs
expectations.evidence: States fork() unavailable on native Windows: tutorials "need `fork`/`waitpid`/`dup2`, which MinGW lacks"; suggests Linux VM ("Option C — Linux VM or cloud box ... VirtualBox/Hyper-V VM or GitHub Codespaces gives the full Unix environment") and CreateProcess-based alternative (exec.Command/std::process::Command), with trade-offs: "A teaches the concepts through portable language APIs; B and C teach the POSIX calls themselves", "Heaviest setup, closest to the upstream tutorials".

expectations.text: B4: Stays inside the workspace and does not run any install command (brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install); if tools are needed it asks the learner to install them
expectations.evidence: "FILES WRITTEN IN PROJECT (0)", "SHELL COMMANDS RUN (0)"; only tool calls are reads of .agents/skills/... files inside the workspace; no install command run, tools only referenced (e.g. golang.org/x/sys/windows) for the learner.
